t: A marine open policy carries a limit per transit of ₹1 crore and a limit per location of ₹2 crore. Goods worth ₹2 crore in a single transit were totally lost by an insured peril. The claim payable is
o: ₹1 crore after applying under-insurance on the balance
e: Liability for goods in any one transit is capped at the limit per transit (per bottom) of ₹1 crore; the location limit applies only to accumulation at a place.

t: A new machine insured for ₹50 lakh under ICC (A) with the Institute Replacement Clause arrives with one component damaged. The component costs ₹2 lakh and ₹30,000 is needed to forward and refit it. The insurer is liable for
o: ₹50 lakh as the machine cannot be used
₹2,30,000 (cost of the part plus forwarding and refitting charges) and not the whole machine value
₹2,30,000 less depreciation for the age of the machine
e: The Institute Replacement Clause limits liability for damage to a part of a new machine to the cost of replacement/repair of that part plus forwarding and refitting charges (plus duty if the sum insured includes duty), never exceeding the insured value.

t: Inland Transit Clause (C) 2010 covers
o: All risks of loss or damage
Named perils including collision, overturning and derailment
e: ITC (A) is all risks, ITC (B) the basic named-perils cover (fire, lightning, breakage of bridges, collision, overturning, derailment) and ITC (C) is restricted to fire and lightning.

t: Under the Insurance Act (Section 64UM) as amended in 2015, a licensed surveyor's report is mandatory for a marine cargo (non-motor) claim exceeding
e: The threshold was raised from ₹20,000 to ₹1 lakh for non-motor claims (₹50,000 for motor) by the 2015 amendment and IRDAI surveyor regulations; smaller claims may be assessed in-house or survey waived.

t: Which of the following is a peril insured under clause 6.1 of ITC Hulls without the due diligence proviso?
o: Violent theft by persons from outside the vessel
e: Clause 6.1 lists perils of the seas, fire/explosion, violent theft by persons from outside the vessel, jettison, piracy, breakdown of nuclear installations, contact with aircraft/land conveyance/dock, earthquake and volcanic eruption; 6.2 perils carry the due diligence proviso.

t: A manufacturer's Sales Turnover Policy is rated at 0.05% on an estimated annual turnover of ₹400 crore. The provisional premium is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). 0.05% of ₹400 crore = ₹20 lakh, payable in advance and adjusted at year end on the actual turnover.

t: A hull policy carries an annual net premium of ₹36.5 lakh and allows a lay-up return of 50% of the pro-rata net premium for each 30 consecutive days laid up not under repair. The vessel is laid up for 60 consecutive days. The return premium is
e: Pro-rata net premium for 60 days = ₹36.5 lakh × 60/365 = ₹6 lakh; 50% return = ₹3 lakh.

t: Basic policy ₹50 lakh; IV policy ₹20 lakh; market value on arrival ₹60 lakh; total loss admitted under the basic policy. The IV claim is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Actual loss ₹60 − ₹50 = ₹10 lakh, 75% = ₹7.5 lakh; 75% of IV sum insured = ₹15 lakh; the lesser ₹7.5 lakh is payable.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: Under the Termination of Transit Clause (Terrorism) 2009, cover against terrorism is available
o: Only while the goods are in the ordinary course of transit, not during storage
Both during transit and during storage at destination
e: The clause restricts strikes/terrorism cover to the ordinary course of transit and terminates it on arrival at the final warehouse or on expiry of the stated days, excluding storage.

t: Goods insured for an agreed value of ₹3,30,000 arrive damaged; gross sound value at destination ₹3,00,000, gross damaged value ₹2,25,000. The claim is
e: Depreciation = 75,000/3,00,000 = 25%; 25% of the agreed value ₹3,30,000 = ₹82,500.

t: Imported goods insured under ICC (A) were discharged at the Indian port but, owing to the importer's delay in clearance, lay in the port warehouse for 75 days before being destroyed by fire. The claim is
o: Not payable, since cover terminated on expiry of 60 days after completion of discharge
Payable, since the goods had not yet reached the final warehouse
Payable, since fire is a named peril
Payable subject to an additional premium for the delay
e: Under the Duration clause (clause 8) the insurance ends on delivery to the final warehouse, on use for storage other than in the ordinary course of transit, or on expiry of 60 days after completion of discharge at the final port, whichever first occurs.

t: Deduction for life insurance premium under Section 80C of the Income Tax Act is available up to an overall limit of:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). ₹1,50,000 aggregate for all 80C items; premium qualifies only up to 10% of the sum assured for policies issued after 1 April 2012.

t: Under an open policy with a limit per bottom of ₹50 lakh, the insured shipped goods worth ₹80 lakh in one vessel which were totally lost. The insurer is liable for
o: Nothing, since the limit was exceeded
₹80 lakh less the premium on the excess value
e: The limit per bottom is the insurer's maximum liability per transit/conveyance; value in excess is borne by the insured unless prior agreement is obtained for a higher limit.

t: Cargo with a contributory value of ₹40 lakh is insured for ₹30 lakh. GA contribution assessed on the cargo is ₹2 lakh. The insurer pays
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Under-insurance applies to GA contributions: ₹2 lakh × 30/40 = ₹1.5 lakh; the insured bears ₹50,000.

t: A consignee incurred ₹40,000 to recondition and re-bag damaged cement so that it could be sold, reducing the loss. The expenditure was incurred at destination after the loss. This is
o: A sue and labour charge, payable over and above the sum insured only if incurred en route
An extra charge, payable with the admitted claim
A salvage charge recoverable from the carrier
e: Charges incurred at destination to ascertain, prove or reduce the loss (reconditioning, survey, sale expenses) are 'extra charges'; sue and labour relates to action to avert or minimise a loss during the transit.

t: 1,000 bags insured for ₹10 lakh were damaged when the vessel stranded. At an intermediate port the goods were sold with the insurer's consent for net proceeds of ₹6 lakh. The claim (salvage loss) is
e: A salvage loss is settled by paying the insured value less the net proceeds of sale: ₹10 lakh − ₹6 lakh = ₹4 lakh.

t: Under COGSA 1925, where loss or damage to goods is not apparent, notice must be given to the carrier within how many days of delivery?
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Article III rule 6 of the Hague Rules: notice of loss must be given at delivery, or within three days if the loss is not apparent, failing which removal is prima facie evidence of delivery in good order.

t: Duty policy sum insured ₹5 lakh; customs duty actually paid ₹4.5 lakh. The cargo is a total loss (admitted under the basic policy). Customs refunded ₹1.5 lakh under Section 22. The duty policy claim is
e: Lesser of duty paid ₹4.5 lakh and sum insured ₹5 lakh = ₹4.5 lakh; less customs refund ₹1.5 lakh = ₹3 lakh.

t: Third-party insurance is compulsory for a motor vehicle used in a public place under which section of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Section 146 makes TP cover compulsory; Section 164 fixes no-fault compensation (₹5 lakh death / ₹2.5 lakh grievous hurt).

t: In which of the following cases is abatement (reduction) of customs duty NOT available under Section 22 of the Customs Act?
o: Goods damaged before or during unloading in India
Goods damaged after unloading but before clearance, by accident not due to the importer
Goods in a bonded warehouse damaged by accident before clearance
Goods damaged in inland transit after clearance for home consumption
e: Abatement is allowed for damage before clearance for home consumption; once goods are cleared the duty is final, and the duty policy must pay without any refund deduction.

t: Damaged cargo insured for ₹3,30,000 lies at an intermediate port. Its value on arrival at destination would be ₹3,00,000, while the cost of reconditioning and forwarding it is ₹3,50,000. The insured gives notice of abandonment. The claim is
o: ₹50,000, the excess of cost over value
e: Goods are a CTL when the cost of recovering, reconditioning and forwarding them to destination would exceed their value on arrival (MIA). The insurer pays the full insured value and takes over the goods.

t: The obligatory cession that Indian general insurers must make to GIC Re is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The obligatory cession was reduced to 4% from 1 April 2022.

t: Under the Marine Insurance Act, 1963 the insurer is liable for any loss
o: Remotely connected with an insured peril
Caused by delay arising from an insured peril
Proximately caused by a peril insured against, but not for any loss not proximately so caused
Caused by wilful misconduct of the assured
e: Section 57 codifies the doctrine of proximate cause: the dominant, effective cause determines liability; losses from delay, wear and tear and wilful misconduct are excluded unless the policy provides otherwise.

t: Non-disclosure of a material fact by the proposer makes the contract:
o: Voidable at the option of the insurer
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Breach of utmost good faith renders the contract voidable, not void; the insurer may elect to avoid it (subject to Section 45 for life).

t: The number of major ports in India under the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 (now the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021) is
e: India has 12 major ports administered by the Central Government (e.g. Mumbai, JNPT, Chennai, Kolkata, Visakhapatnam); other ports are minor ports under State Governments.

t: A corporate agent may tie up with a maximum of how many insurers in each line of business?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 3 to 9 insurers per category (life, general, health) by the 2022 amendment to the Corporate Agents Regulations.

t: Wheat is insured under ICC (A) for ₹10 lakh. The insured's agents spent ₹3 lakh as sue and labour charges to protect the cargo from an insured peril. The voyage continued and the cargo later became a total loss covered by the policy. Total claim payable is
e: Sue and labour charges properly incurred are recoverable in addition to the sum insured even where a total loss follows: ₹10 lakh + ₹3 lakh = ₹13 lakh.

t: Which of the following is a change introduced by the Institute Cargo Clauses 2009 as compared with the 1982 clauses?
o: The 60-day period after discharge was reduced to 30 days
The word 'servants' was replaced by 'employees' and the term 'goods' by 'subject-matter insured'
ICC (C) was widened to include earthquake
War risks were included in ICC (A)
e: The 2009 revision modernised the wording (employees, subject-matter insured), advanced the attachment of transit to first movement for loading, narrowed the unseaworthiness and insolvency exclusions and added the terrorism motive clause.

t: Under clause 7 of ICC 2009, loss caused by any person acting from a political, ideological or religious motive is
o: Excluded from the cargo clauses and insurable only under the Institute Strikes Clauses
Covered under all three sets of clauses
Covered under the Institute War Clauses
e: Clause 7.4 was added in 2009 to exclude such acts along with terrorism (7.3); both are bought back under the Institute Strikes Clauses (Cargo) 2009.
